sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: An erect annual in the carrot family, often 0.9–1.8 m tall, with finely divided leaves and broad umbels of small white flowers. It is native from Macaronesia and the Mediterranean region to Turkmenistan and the Arabian Peninsula and has been introduced elsewhere.

sections.title: Safety and uses
sections.text: Its furanocoumarins can cause a phototoxic skin reaction after sun exposure. Horticultural sources also list the plant as toxic to dogs, cats and horses. The sources consulted do not establish a specific food use.
